questions.question: Recreate the styling shown below using a tag selector.
questions.instructions: Use a tag selector to make all paragraph elements blue.
questions.explanation:
A **tag selector** uses the HTML element name. Use `p { color: blue; }` to select all `

` elements and make them blue.

questions.question: Recreate the styling shown below using a class selector.
questions.instructions: Use a class selector to give all elements with class 'highlight' a yellow background.
questions.explanation: A **class selector** starts with a period (`.`). Use `.highlight { background-color: yellow; }` to select all elements with `class="highlight"`.

questions.question: Recreate the styling shown below using an ID selector.
questions.instructions: Use an ID selector to make the element with id 'main-title' large (32px), bold, and blue.
questions.explanation: An **ID selector** starts with a hash (`#`). Use `#main-title { font-size: 32px; font-weight: bold; color: blue; }` to select the element with `id="main-title"`.

questions.question: Recreate the styling shown below using a descendant selector.
questions.instructions: Use a descendant selector to make all paragraphs inside divs italic.
questions.explanation:
A **descendant selector** uses a space between selectors. Use `div p { font-style: italic; }` to select all `

` elements that are anywhere inside `

` elements.

questions.question: Recreate the styling shown below using a direct child selector.
questions.instructions: Use a direct child selector to add a hotpink border to only the direct children of the unordered list with the class 'menu'.
questions.explanation: A **direct child selector** uses the `>` symbol. Use `ul.menu > li { border: 1px solid hotpink; }` to select only `<li>` elements that are direct children of `<ul>` elements with the class 'menu'.

questions.question: Recreate the styling shown below using a grouping selector.
questions.instructions: Use a grouping selector to apply the same red color to both h1 and h2 elements.
questions.explanation: A **grouping selector** uses a comma (`,`). Use `h1, h2 { color: red; }` to apply the same styles to both all `<h1>` elements and all `<h2>` elements.
